plan.summary:
New `Record` IDs now use UUIDv7, which sorts by creation time, instead of random UUIDv4.

- `Cargo.toml` swaps the `uuid` feature `v4` for `v7`.
- `Record::new` calls `Uuid::now_v7()`.
- `Cargo.lock` adds the transitive dependencies that follow from the feature change.

Existing records keep their old IDs. Only new records get time-ordered IDs.
plan.riskRationale: Small change: one feature flag and one constructor call. The `v4` feature is removed, so any other `Uuid::new_v4()` call in the crate would fail to compile. Existing stored IDs are unchanged.
plan.storyArc: The PR enables the `v7` feature of the `uuid` crate. It then uses `Uuid::now_v7()` when a `Record` is created. The lockfile changes follow from the manifest change.

noise.reason: Lockfile churn that follows the `uuid` feature change in Cargo.toml (adds `js-sys` to a dependency list).

topics.title: Record IDs use time-ordered UUIDv7
topics.narrativeBrief: How do new records get their IDs, and what must change in the manifest to allow it? Connect the `v4` to `v7` feature swap in `Cargo.toml` to the `Uuid::now_v7()` call in `Record::new`. Verify that no other code in the crate still calls `new_v4`.
